title: Gaussian affine integral identity
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a\in\mathbb R^n$ and $b,c,v\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $c\ge 0$, $v\ge 0$, and $b^2+c^2=v^2$. For every strongly measurable function $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, integrating $f(a+bZ+cW)$ over independent standard Gaussian vectors $Z,W\in\mathbb R^n$ gives the same integral as integrating $f(a+vY)$ over a standard Gaussian vector $Y\in\mathbb R^n$.
